messages:
elyse-support: heads-up — customer `acme-pay` on Dedicated pool `eu-west-1-d-5` reported a sudden throughput drop ~13:02 UTC, their tail latency and tokens/sec both fell ~60%.
sam-runtime: ugh, same pool as the new prefill policy change we rolled last week? @raj-sre can you pull the autoscale + batcher traces?
raj-sre: pulling metrics now. I see a spike in microfill count and a sustained increase in small microbatches starting 12:58 UTC. Looks like continuous-batcher is emitting lots of <8 token microbatches.
elyse-support: customer says they didn't change client traffic pattern — they saw normal QPS but each request now takes longer and we hit 429-ish throttles from the scheduler.
maria-cs: they're also seeing repeated charge errors in client logs (generic 429/503 mix). Billing team flagged no invoice issues on our side.
sam-runtime: likely scheduling packing inefficiency. Possibly our `max_batch_tokens` was reduced in the canary. Can someone check canary config and kernel selection rollouts?
raj-sre: confirmed: config `prefill_policy: aggressive` was enabled in canary pool at 2026-03-17T11:45:12Z and propagated to eu-west-1-d-5 at 12:30Z. It decreases prefill size to favor latency, but in presence of many short requests it increases microburst count.
elyse-support: customer provided a repro curl: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"txn status","max_tokens":32}'``` they are doing many small prompts.
sam-runtime: that fits. Aggressive prefill + continuous-batcher -> many tiny batches = low GPU packing efficiency -> throughput collapse. Need roll-forward mitigation: revert prefill_policy or bump `max_batch_tokens` and increase pack window.
raj-sre: quick mitigation steps I can do: 1) disable prefill_policy override for that dedicated pool, 2) increase `pack_window_ms` from 8 -> 20 for the pool, 3) temporarily raise `max_batch_tokens` from 2048 -> 4096 for model family. Which should I prioritize?
maria-cs: customer prefers minimal impact to latency — they'd accept a transient bump in cost while we stabilize. They asked for ETA ~30-45m.
elyse-support: can you also whitelist their pool from autoscaler aggressive downscale? They've seen abrupt slot reclaim that worsened the problem.
raj-sre: yep. I'll pause aggressive downscale and apply pack_window change first — should see improvement in ~2-3 min after config rollout.
sam-runtime: add one more: enable KV-cache warmup for their sessions and extend cache TTL to avoid repeated prefill overhead (helps for repeated short prompts).
ops-bot: deploy-trigger: config-update started for pool eu-west-1-d-5 by raj-sre (change-id: cfg-20260317-331). :rotating_light:
raj-sre: rolled pack_window to 20ms and bumped max_batch_tokens in the family. Monitoring: moving average tokens/sec climbed 35% in first minute, median latency trending down.
elyse-support: customer confirms latency regressing back towards normal at 13:14 UTC. They still saw a couple 429s, but overall throughput improving. :relieved:
maria-cs: can we schedule a follow-up postmortem? they'd like notes on config change timeline and recommended stable defaults for dedicated pools with many short prompts.
sam-runtime: yes — I'll open an incident doc and include suggested safe defaults: prefills: conservative, pack_window 15-25ms, max_batch_tokens >= 4096 for L2 models, and autoscale downscale cooldown 3m.
raj-sre: filing the incident (INC-20260317-45) with traces and commands used. Also tagging runtime-config team to block aggressive prefill policy from auto-propagating to dedicated pools without manual approval.
elyse-support: thanks all. customer appreciated the quick fix, moving to monitoring-only. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-complete: config-update cfg-20260317-331 finished at 2026-03-17T13:16:02Z."
